chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'When do I pray the two rak'ahs of Fajr?' He said, 'When the dawn breaks, which is what the Arabs call as-sadeeq (the true dawn).' As for what has been narrated that their time is with the dawn or after the dawn, like what he narrated:

key_terms.الصَّدِيعَ: The true dawn (specific type of dawn)
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: The two voluntary rak'ahs of Fajr prayer
key_terms.وَقْتُهُمَا: Their time (referring to the prayer time)

ai.seo_question: When should the two voluntary rak'ahs of Fajr be prayed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the specific window for the two sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr, defining the time as 'as-sadeeq' (the second dawn) rather than the first false dawn. It resolves apparent contradictions in other narrations by distinguishing between the onset of prayer time and the precise moment for these voluntary acts, reflecting the Shia emphasis on adhering to the Prophet’s detailed temporal guidance.
